senses.gloss:
नितततपम् नितततपम्, ind., Ved. an ono-
matopoetic word to denote the speech of a stutterer.

नितन् नि-तन्, cl. 8. P. A. -तनोति, -नुते,
-तनितुम्, Ved. to pervade, penetrate, pierce; to
cause to grow downwards (as a shoot, root, &c.).

नि-तत्नी, f., Ved. a species of plant; N. of an
Iṣṭakā; N. of one of the seven stars of the asterism
Kṛttikā.

नि-तान, अस्, m., Ved. the shoot of a plant which
grows downwards; N. of a man with the patronymic
Māruta.

नितप् नि-तप्, cl. 1. P. -तपति, -तप्तुम्,
Ved. to emit heat downwards; to consume.

नितम् नि-तम्, Caus. P. -तमयति, &c., Ved.
to choke, suffocate.

नि-तान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, extraordinary, excessive,
exceeding, much, considerable; (अम्), ind. exceed-
ingly, excessively, very, much, in a high degree.
—नितान्तावृक्ष (˚त-अव्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, excessively
treeless.
नितान्त नि-तान्त. See नि-तम् above.

नितम्ब नि-तम्ब, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt.
तम्ब्, probably connected with rt. स्तम्भ्), the
buttocks or posteriors, especially of a woman, (in
this sense generally नितम्बौ, m. du.); the cir-
cumference of the hip and loins; the ridge or side
or protuberant flank or swell of a mountain [cf. गिरि-
नितम्ब]; a precipice; the sloping bank or shore
of a river; the shoulder; a particular position of the
hands in dancing; (आ), f. a form of Durgā.
—नि-
तम्ब-ता, f. the state of having large hips.
—नि-
तम्ब-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having beautiful buttocks or
hips, καλλίπυγος; (ती), f. a woman.
—नितम्ब-
विम्ब, अस्, आ, अम्, having Vimba-like hips.

नितम्बिन्, ई, इनी, इ (at the end of a comp.),
having buttocks; having beautiful hips; having
graceful slopes, having beautiful sides (as a moun-
tain); (इनी), f. a woman with large and handsome
hips.

नितम्भू नितम्भू, ऊस्, m., N. of a person
mentioned in Mahā-bh. Anuśāsana-p. 1765; (per-
haps for नित्यम्-भू.)

नितराम् नि-तराम्, ind. (fr. नि with the
comparative affix), downwards, towards the lower
part (Ved.); in a low tone (Ved.); completely,
wholly, entirely; much, extremely, excessively, in a
high degree; in an especial manner, always, con-
tinually, eternally; at all events; certainly; [cf. Angl.
Sax. nidher; Old Germ. nidar.]

नितल नि-तल, अम्, n. one of the seven
divisions of the lower regions. See पाताल.

नितिक्त नि-तिक्त, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. तिज् with
नि), Ved. excited, roused up.

नितुद् नि-तुद्, cl. 6. P. A. -तुदति, -ते, -तोत्-
तुम्, Ved. to pierce, penetrate, pierce into; to goad;
(Sāy.) to incite or pain vehemently, or to issue forth
(= नितरां व्यथयति or निर्-गच्छति).
नि-तोद, अस्, m. piercing, a prick, puncture, hole.
नि-तोदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. piercing, penetrating.

नितृद् नि-तृद्, cl. 7. P. A. -तृणत्ति, -तृन्त्ते,
-तर्दितुम्, Ved. to pierce, penetrate, cleave in two.

नितॄ नि-तॄ, cl. 6. P. -तिरति, -तरितुम्, -त-
रीतुम्, Ved. to dispel, subdue, overpower, obstruct.

नित्य नित्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नि), own (Ved.);
continual, perpetual, regularly repeated, constant,
uninterrupted, endless, eternal, everlasting; invariable,
regular, fixed, regularly prescribed, inevitable, not op-
tional, (opposed to काम्य &c.); necessary, obligatory,
essential; ordinary, usual, (opposed to नैमित्तिक,
unusual, produced by an unusual cause); constantly
dwelling in, perpetually engaged in, (often at the end
of a comp., e. g. अरण्य-नित्य, constantly dwelling
in a forest; तपो-नित्य, engaged in constant penance);
(with समास) a necessary compound which cannot
be resolved without losing its meaning, because the
separate ideas have merged in one, as in जमद्-अग्नि;
(with स्वरित) = जात्य, the primary or independent
Svarita, as opposed to the secondary or dependent;
(अस्), m. the ocean; (आ), f. an epithet of Durgā; a
Śakti or form of Durgā; an epithet of the goddess Ma-
nasā; (अम्), n. constant and indispensable rite or act;
(अम्), ind. always, ever, daily, constantly, continually,
perpetually, everlastingly, eternally; न नित्यम्, not
always, never, (in Manu VI. 8. नित्यम् अन्-आदाता =
never a receiver.)
—नित्य-कर्मन्, अ, n. or नित्य-
क्रिया, f. constant act or duty, as observance of the
five great sacrifices or any daily and necessary rite.
—नित्य-कृत्य, अम्, n. regular and necessary act
or ceremony; daily or regular act or routine.
—नित्य-
गति, इस्, इस्, इ, moving continually; (इस्), m. air or
wind, the god of wind.
—नित्य-जात, अस्, आ, अम्,
constantly born.
—नित्य-ता, f. perpetuity, eternity,
continuance, continual repetition, (as मैथुन-
नित्यता, continually repeated coitus); perseverance;
necessity.
—नित्य-त्व, अम्, n. invariableness, per-
petuity, eternity; endurance; inevitableness, neces-
sity.
—नित्य-दा, ind. always, ever, perpetually, con-
stantly, eternally, at all times.
—नित्य-दान, अम्, n.
daily alms-giving.
—नित्य-धृत्, त्, त्, त्, constantly
bearing or maintaining, observing daily duties (?).
—नित्य-धृत, अस्, आ, अम्, constantly maintained
or kept up.
—नित्य-नाथ-सिद्ध, अस्, m., N. of
an author.
—नित्य-नियम, अस्, m. fixed rule,
constant observance.
—नित्य-नैमित्तिक, अम्, or
नित्य-नैमित्तिकं कर्म, n. any regularly re-
curring occasional act or ceremony or any rite con-
stantly performed to accomplish some object, as
Śrāddhas at fixed lunar periods.
—नित्य-परिवृत,
अस्, m., N. of a Buddha.
—नित्य-परीक्षण, अम्,
n. constant investigation or inspection.
—नित्य-पूजा-
यन्त्र, अम्, n. a kind of amulet.
—नित्य-प्रलय,
अस्, m. the constant dissolution of living beings.
—नित्य-भाव, अस्, m. the state of being eternal,
eternity.
—नित्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, formed of or
consisting of anything eternal, eternal.
—नित्य-
युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, always busy, ever engaged in.
—नित्य-यौवन, अम्, n. perpetual youth; (अस्, ई,
अम्), ever or always young; (आ), f. an epithet of
Draupadī.
—नित्यर्तु (˚य-ऋ), उस्, उस्, उ, regularly
recurring at the seasons, annual.
—नित्य-वत्स, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. always possessing a calf; (आ), f. a par-
ticular form of Sāma supplication; (अम्), n., N. of
several Sāmans.
—नित्य-वित्रस्त, अस्, m. ‘constantly
scared,’ N. of an antelope.
—नित्य-वैकुण्ठ, अस्,
m., N. of a particular residence of Viṣṇu, the
heaven of Viṣṇu.
—नित्य-व्यय, अस्, आ, अम्, always
expending, constantly disbursing; (आ), f. always ex-
pending, ever laying out.
—नित्य-शङ्कित, अस्, आ,
[]
अम्, perpetually alarmed, always suspicious.
—नित्य-
शय, अस्, आ, अम्, always sleeping or reclining.
—नित्य-
शस्, ind. always, continually, constantly, eternally.
—नित्य-संहृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, always exulting
or triumphant; always rivalling one another, (in this
sense संहृष्ट = सङ्घृष्ट.)
—नित्य-सम,
अस्, m. the assertion that all things remain the same (?).
—नित्य-समास, see नित्य.
—नित्य-सिद्ध, अस्,
आ, अम्, ‘ever perfect,’ a Jaina predicate of the soul.
—नित्य-स्तोत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. receiving perpetual
praise, constantly lauded.
—नित्य-स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
constantly bathing or making ablutions.
—नित्यान-
ध्याय (˚य-अन्˚), अस्, m. invariable suspension of
repetition of the Vedas, (a term applied to periods
when the perusal of the Vedas is invariably prohibited,
as the day of full moon, new moon, the eighth and
fourteenth days of the half month.)
—नित्यानन्द
(˚य-आन्˚), अस्, m. eternal happiness.
—नित्यानन्द-
रसोदधि (˚स-उद्˚), इस्, m. ‘ocean of the essence of
eternal joy,’ God.
—नित्यानन्दाश्रम (˚द-आश्˚),
अस्, m., N. of a commentator.
—नित्यानित्य (˚य-अन्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, eternal and perishable, permanent and
temporary.
—नित्यायुक्त (˚य-आय्˚), अस्, m., N. of a
Bodhi-sattva; (also read नित्योयुक्त; cf. नित्यो-
द्युक्त.)
—नित्यारित्र (˚य-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
having (its) own oars, ever fitted with oars (i. e.
according to Sāy. with priests).
—नित्योत्क्षिप्त-
हस्त (˚य-उत्˚), अस्, m. ‘who always raises his hand,’
N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
—नित्योदित (˚य-उद्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a man.
—नित्योद्युक्त (˚य-उद्˚), अस्, m.,
N. of a Bodhi-sattva; [cf. नित्यायुक्त.]

नित्यज् नि-त्यज्, cl. 1. P. -त्यजति, -त्यक्तुम्,
Ved. to scare or drive away.

1. नीत, अस्, आ, अम्, led, guided, conducted; brought,
reduced; gained, obtained; well-behaved, correct,
modest; (अम्), n. wealth; corn, grain; [cf. असु-न्˚,
दुर्-न्˚, &c.]

2. नीत, अस्, आ, अम्, entered, gone to; (Sāy.) =
नितराम् प्राप्त.
नीत नीत, नीति, &c. See p. 511, col. 2.

नीत्त नी-त्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for नि-दत्त fr. rt.
1. दा with नि), Ved. given.

नीति, इस्, f. guiding, guidance, directing, direction,
management; manner of conducting one's self, con-
duct, propriety; right or moral or prudent behaviour,
prudent counsel, policy, political wisdom or science,
political economy, state policy, statesmanship, the
administration of government; moral philosophy,
ethics, precepts for prudent and moral behaviour,
prudence, Prudence or Polity personified [cf. नय];
leading or bringing to, obtaining, acquirement, acqui-
sition; presenting, offering; relation, support; [cf.
अग्र-णीति, अदब्ध-न्˚, असु-न्˚, ऋजु-न्˚, &c.]
—नीति-
कथा, f. any work on moral or political science, a
discourse on political economy.
—नीति-कुशल, अस्,
आ, अम्, conversant with political science, skilful in
human affairs, a good statesman.
—नीति-घोष, अस्,
m., N. of the car of Bṛhas-pati.
—नीति-ज्ञ, अस्, आ,
अम्, knowing what is right especially in government,
sagacious, politic, prudent; (अस्), m. a prudent
statesman or soldier, a politician.
—नीति-दोष, अस्,
m. error of conduct, mistake in policy.
—नीति-
निष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, versed in political or moral
science.
—नीति-प्रदीप, अस्, m. ‘the light of pru-
dent behaviour,’ N. of a collection of verses attributed
to Vetāla-bhaṭṭa.
—नीति-मञ्जरी, f., N. of a work
on morality or right behaviour.
—नीति-मत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, knowing the rules of moral or prudent
behaviour, moral, prudent, eminent for political
wisdom.
—नीति-रत्न, अम्, n. ‘the jewel of mora-
lity,’ N. of a collection of verses attributed to Vara-
ruci.
—नीति-वाक्यामृत (˚य-अम्˚), अम्, n. ‘nectar
of discourse on morality or prudent behaviour,’ N.
of a work.
—नीति-विद्, त्, m. a politician, any one
versed in political science, a statesman.
—नीति-विद्या,
f. moral or political science, political economy; [cf.
नीति-शास्त्र.]
—नीति-विषय, अस्, m. the sphere of
morality or prudent conduct.
—नीति-वीज, अम्, n. a
germ or source of intrigue.
—नीति-वेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
knowing policy, a politician.
—नीति-व्यतिक्रम, अस्,
m. error of conduct, transgression of the rules of
moral or political science.
—नीति-शतक, अम्, n. the
hundred verses on morality by Bhartṛ-hari.
—नीति-
शास्त्र, अम्, n. the science of ethics or politics, any
work on political ethics or morals.
—नीति-सङ्क-
लन, अम्, n. ‘collection of rules for moral conduct
or prudent behaviour,’ N. of a modern work.
—नीति-
सार, अस्, m. or अम्, n. the essence of political or
moral science; (अम्), n. a special work on this
subject by Ghaṭa-karpara.

नीत्वा, ind. having led or conducted or guided;
having taken; having passed or spent (as time).

नीतमिश्र नीत-मिश्र, अस्, आ, अम् (नीत =
नव-नीत), Ved. not yet become butter, (said of
दधि.)
